title: On the Discipline of Being Findable
script: Narrator: [wry] There is a particular exhaustion, rarely named precisely, that comes not from working too much but from being perpetually available to work, which turns out to be an entirely different affliction.

Narrator: [analytical] I used to conflate the two, assuming that if I merely reduced my hours, the exhaustion would recede proportionally, and it never quite did, which puzzled me for longer than I'd like to admit.

Narrator: [reflective] What finally clarified things was noticing that my shoulders tensed the instant I glimpsed a notification, regardless of whether I opened it, regardless even of whether I was technically off duty at the time.
Narrator: [candid] The mere possibility of a demand, it turns out, exacts nearly the same toll as the demand itself, a discovery that felt less like insight than accusation.

Narrator: [thoughtful] We've built, almost accidentally, an economy that prizes findability as though it were a virtue indistinguishable from diligence, when in fact they share almost nothing beyond a superficial resemblance.
Narrator: [firm] Diligence is what you do with your attention once it's engaged. Findability is merely surrendering the right to decide when it gets engaged at all.

Narrator: [honest] I spent years mistaking the second for the first, priding myself on rapid replies at inconvenient hours as though responsiveness were itself an achievement rather than simply an erosion I'd stopped noticing.

Narrator: [determined] So I've instituted something almost comically modest: a window, roughly ninety minutes each evening, during which the phone is physically elsewhere, out of both reach and eyeline.
Narrator: [wry] The withdrawal, I confess, was considerably more acute than I'd anticipated for something this small, which itself told me everything about how deep the habit had rooted.

Narrator: [warmly] Ninety minutes is a modest ambition, I realize, hardly the stuff of a manifesto. But it's the first ninety minutes in years during which nobody, anywhere, could summon my attention without my prior consent.

quiz.question: What kind of exhaustion does the narrator distinguish from simply working too much?
options: Physical exhaustion from exercise
The exhaustion of being perpetually available to work
Exhaustion from lack of sleep
Exhaustion from travel
quiz.explanation: She distinguishes exhaustion from overwork from the distinct exhaustion of being perpetually available.

quiz.question: What did the narrator notice about her body when she glimpsed a notification?
options: Nothing at all
Her shoulders tensed, regardless of whether she opened it or was off duty
She felt immediate relief
She fell asleep
quiz.explanation: She noticed her shoulders tensed at the mere sight of a notification, regardless of opening it or being off duty.

quiz.question: How does the narrator distinguish diligence from findability?
options: They are essentially the same thing
Diligence is what you do with engaged attention; findability is surrendering the right to decide when it engages
Findability is more valuable than diligence
Diligence requires more technology
quiz.explanation: She defines diligence as directing engaged attention, while findability surrenders the right to decide when attention engages at all.

quiz.question: What modest habit has the narrator instituted?
options: Deleting all her apps permanently
A roughly ninety-minute window each evening when her phone is physically out of reach
Working only mornings
Turning off her phone for a full week
quiz.explanation: She has instituted a roughly ninety-minute evening window during which her phone is physically elsewhere.

quiz.question: What did the intensity of her withdrawal reveal to the narrator?
options: That the habit was shallow and easy to break
How deeply the habit of constant availability had rooted
That she should abandon the experiment
That ninety minutes was too short to matter
quiz.explanation: The unexpectedly acute withdrawal revealed to her how deeply the habit of findability had rooted.
